Tracks partition-creation rate — use this to confirm whether the interval/list partitioning scheme is keeping up with data volume, and whether old partitions are candidates for archiving or purging.
◆ C. ASM / Storage Capacity
ASM Disk Groups total / free / usable free per diskgroup
"Usable Free" already accounts for the mirroring/redundancy overhead (normal/high redundancy) — it's the number that reflects real available capacity, not raw free space. If this database doesn't use ASM (filesystem storage), this stays empty — that's expected, not an error.
◆ D. CPU, Memory & I/O Capacity
🖥 CPU Capacity
🧠 Memory Capacity
💽 I/O Capacity
avg read latency — the real capacity/headroom signal
📁 Datafile Count vs. Structural Limit
Refresh to load
Every database has a hard ceiling on the number of datafiles it can ever have (the db_files parameter). Running out blocks any further tablespace/datafile growth even if disk space is free.
◆ E. Sessions & Resource Limits
👥 Sessions, Processes & Locks — Peak % of Hard Limit
Refresh to load
Hitting these limits causes ORA-00018/ORA-00020 (too many sessions/processes) — an application outage, not a storage issue, but just as much a capacity problem.

Anomaly Detection AI
Watches your database 24/7 for unusual behaviour — Scanning…
🧠
What is Anomaly Detection?
This panel monitors real-time Oracle metrics and compares them against a learned baseline. When something deviates — like a tablespace growing too fast, or too many queries being parsed without reuse — it fires an alert. The anomaly score is a number from 0–1: anything above 0.4 (the dashed red line) is flagged. A score of 1.0 = extreme deviation from normal.

Add Oracle Database


      
      


      

        

          
        

        

          
        

        

          
          
          
⚠ Enter host:port of the running server.js backend (e.g. http://192.168.2.100:8080).

        

        

          

            
          

          

            
          

        

        
💡 Enter the Oracle DB credentials below. The proxy server will connect to this database directly.

        

          

            
          

          

            
          

        

        
        

          💡 SYS detected — for SYS you must specify the privilege in the username field:

          sys as sysdba  or  sys as sysoper

          The server strips the qualifier and passes the correct Oracle privilege automatically.
        

        

          

            
          

          
          

            ✅ Correct format: (DESCRIPTION=(ADDRESS=(PROTOCOL=TCP)(HOST=your-host)(PORT=1521))(CONNECT_DATA=(SERVICE_NAME=your-service)))

            ❌ Wrong: ALIAS=(DESCRIPTION=...) — alias prefix is auto-stripped but avoid if possible.
